newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT cuts jobs at Leykam.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT cuts jobs at Leykam.

text.p: Dutch paper and packaging group NV Koninklijke KNP BT said on Wednesday it would cut 1,000 jobs of a total 4,600 at its majority-owned paper division KNP Leykam.

"The intended reorganisation, which will result in a structural cost cut of 100 million guilders per year, is part of KNP BT's strategy to turn KNP Leykam into one of the most competitive producers of woodfree coated paper," KNP BT said in a statement.
KNP Leykam is 92 percent owned by KNP BT. The paper group is currently in the middle of a 1.2 billion guilders investment programme.
This includes a one billion guilder investment in a new paper plant in Austria and a 200 million injection in a paper plant in the southern Dutch city of Maastricht.

KNP BT said the job cuts would take place until the end of 1999. About half of the job losses would be caused by decreasing overhead and the other half by strategic investments and productivity improvements.
It will cut more than 500 jobs in Austria, where four smaller paper production plants will be dismantled over the next few years to be replaced by the new factory.
Another 350 jobs will be axed in the Netherlands, 110 in Belgium and an unspecified number in the rest of Europe.
KNP BT said forced dismissals were inevitable to realise the Leykam restructuring and added it had started talks with trade unions and works councils.

The group said last September it was seeking a strategic partner for its KNP Leykam division, to create economies of scale and synergy profits. In today's statement it said it expected to find such a partner before the end of this year.

KNP Leykam posted 1995 net profit of 344 million guilders. In the first half of 1996 it suffered an operating loss of 24 million guilders, compared with a profit of 183 million in the year-earlier period.
